overallNote: Partial recovery: as of 11:36 PM Microsoft says adjusting traffic protocols, redistributing traffic and selectively blocking some traffic is bringing partial recovery in the regions where it's been applied. Not resolved; access may still be intermittent. Microsoft says Teams is restored.

services.name: Exchange Online / Outlook
services.note: Partial recovery in regions where Microsoft has applied traffic changes; still intermittent elsewhere.

services.name: Microsoft Teams
services.note: Microsoft says its fixes restored Teams service health. Sign-in/connectivity may still be affected for some users.

services.name: SharePoint Online / OneDrive
services.note: Named as possibly affected by the connectivity issue.

services.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
services.note: Named as possibly affected; ~6,000 Downdetector reports at peak.

services.name: Planner / To Do / Power BI / Print
services.note: Reported failing for some users as the outage spread. Microsoft's affected list also now includes Intune.

services.name: M365 admin center / status page
services.note: Admin portal and status page had loading errors earlier; status page is back online.

services.name: Azure
services.note: Not named in this incident. Check Azure status for anything separate.

timeline.text: Microsoft investigating problems reaching Exchange Online mailboxes through several connection methods in the Americas (EX1550543).
Confirmed the issue may affect Microsoft 365 connectivity for users in any region.
Part of the infrastructure is under elevated load across multiple regions (MO1550821 opened).
Began redistributing connection traffic across worldwide infrastructure to balance load.
Load isn't from traffic: servers failing automated health checks are dropping out, straining the rest.
Paused all deployments, moving traffic off affected infrastructure, restarting affected servers.
Testing a configuration change for the health-check failures; restart of all affected servers started.
No recent change linked to the start; a component that processes server health is suspected. Steps taken to stop more servers being hit.
New health-check method returned a subset of servers to service; applying it more broadly and preparing automated recovery.
Microsoft says Teams service health restored.
Restarting and validating servers; assessing whether reverting some recent configuration updates could speed recovery.
Actions so far haven't given the expected relief. A core process on affected servers is getting overwhelmed; isolating servers to validate a recovery path.
Microsoft 365 status page back online, showing 'Service degradation on Microsoft 365 (Business or Enterprise)'.
Shifting traffic to alternate routes where possible and seeing limited recovery; still restoring capacity and investigating why servers stopped responding.
Microsoft warns access may return gradually because of a backlog.
Microsoft returning a portion of affected servers to service; they're stable so far. Not yet declared resolved.
Phishing warning: expect fake 'reset your password' emails/texts as Outlook comes back. Microsoft won't ask for this.

Returned servers can go unresponsive again once they receive traffic. Microsoft is analyzing diagnostics, temporarily limiting which types of traffic reach affected infrastructure in some locations, and rebuilding some servers with a previous configuration to test whether that stops it.
Microsoft reviewed known impact scenarios and revised the list of impacted services and features in MO1550821 (admin center / status.cloud.microsoft).

Microsoft has begun reverting a recent network configuration change that correlates with the start of impact and is monitoring whether it helps recovery. Will expand the server rebuilds if they show positive results.
Microsoft says the overloaded process on affected servers is the one handling secure connections, which made the servers stop processing requests. Rollback of the network change continues.

Microsoft reports positive results restarting affected infrastructure and recovering server availability in an isolated way; monitoring those portions to verify stability, which it expects to support broader recovery.
Microsoft applying infrastructure capacity improvements where possible to support traffic in regions coming back online; monitoring results to pick next actions for all affected regions.
Microsoft says the changes applied to improve serviceability are not taking as expected; identifying alternate workstreams to increase capacity given sustained traffic-management imbalances.

Investigating the sustained traffic-management imbalances: reviewing traffic flows and affected infrastructure to optimize routing, and verifying the reasons for service failures to develop specific fixes.

Microsoft continuing to improve server stability by adjusting traffic protocols, redistributing traffic and applying strategic traffic blocking; seeing partial recovery in regions where these measures were applied.

Microsoft says it has multiple workstreams under way to reduce impact, clear its current blocker and return portions of infrastructure to a healthy state; fuller details in MO1550821 in the admin center.
Microsoft still recovering its frontend servers while applying further traffic optimizations to improve stability and add capacity; details in MO1550821.
